newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in slow trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar amid ample liquidity and slow late trading on Monday, dealers said.
They said volume was fairly thin, with no clear sign of where rates were going to head next.

"There is no momentum at all. There was small buying of three- and six-month swaps on minor spillover from Thailand, apart from that we don't have much action today," one dealer said. Spot rupiah was at 2,428.00/28.25 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,427.5/28.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,427.75/28.00 and 2,427.5/28.0, respectively.

Dealers said liquidity was ample in the afternoon and overnight money fell to seven percent from 13.0. But there was no dollar buying as dealers said early fears of possible tightening on Tuesday due to weekly tax payments had subsided.
One state bank dealer said Tuesday's tax payments were likely to be smaller than last Friday and would have no significant impact on the market.
Overnight swap was at 0.35/0.35 and tom/next at 0.30/0.33.
The market also shrugged off weekend riots in east Java where a Moslem crowd burned shops, a Protestant church and a Buddhist temple on Saturday. The area was peaceful on Sunday.
Dealers said offshore operators took the incident in their stride and would only have been concerned if there was violence in Jakarta.
One-month swaps were at 12.25/13.00, two at 25.50/26.50, three at 39.5/40.0 and six at 79.5/81.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,422/2,614 and its conversion band also by one point to 2,422/2,470 on Monday.
